task: Upgrade the approved VX Builder Core with a curated visual Library 2.0 for sections, elements and page templates: lightweight semantic thumbnails, search/category filtering, contextual insertion and larger bounded previews, while preserving canonical preset/page-template/runtime authorities, product-profile capability filtering and Guarded Freedom.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Library 2.0 sits directly on the authoring path and can influence what merchants insert into canonical Page documents. Strong behavioral proof is justified for capability filtering, bounded preview rendering, insertion integrity and performance. Formal verification would add disproportionate cost because the slice introduces no new transactional, persistence or concurrent protocol authority.

deferredTechniques.reason: The gallery state is UI/filter driven; targeted state matrices and canonical insertion validation provide better assurance-to-cost ratio.
No payment, inventory or distributed consistency protocol changes; persistence and runtime authorities remain unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: Sections, elements and page templates use a shared VX Library visual language with lightweight semantic thumbnails instead of generic registry rows or live runtime instantiation.
Section Presets expose search, meaningful curated categories and a bounded larger preview before one-click insertion.
Element insertion cards expose recognizable semantic previews while continuing to list only structurally valid and product-profile/capability-allowed components.
Page Templates use the same visual card/preview language and retain existing apply/create-new-page authority.
Factory Section Presets remain source-controlled canonical preset material; tenant Saved Blocks remain a separate merchant-owned library.
Every insertion/application continues through existing preset/page-template materialization and validation functions; no second document, renderer, persistence or publish path is introduced.
Preview generation is bounded metadata/CSS composition only and must not instantiate one StorefrontRuntimeRenderer per Library card.
VX Shop may expose commerce library items, while the shared Core classification/preview system remains product-agnostic and compatible with future VX Site capability profiles.
Mobile Library remains polished and inspectable, but Desktop remains the full authoring authority and no mobile-only content/page model is created.
invariants: Template -> Page Preset -> Section Preset -> Component remains canonical.
A Library preview is presentation metadata only and can never become insertion/persistence authority.
Factory presets and Saved Blocks are never merged into one ownership model.
Capability and parent/child compatibility remain fail-closed before insertion.
Library search/filtering cannot reveal or insert a component hidden by the active product profile or entitlement.
No unbounded number of live runtime renderers is mounted for thumbnails or previews.
Inserted preset nodes receive canonical fresh identities and remain fully editable native Builder content.
Guarded Freedom continues to prohibit arbitrary HTML/JavaScript and unbounded freeform layout primitives.

alternatives.summary: Render every preset and element card with a full live StorefrontRuntimeRenderer miniature.
alternatives.reason: High runtime/DOM cost, duplicate interaction complexity and explicit conflict with the roadmap's bounded thumbnail contract.

alternatives.summary: Build a shared semantic Library descriptor/preview layer over existing canonical preset, component and page-template authorities.
alternatives.reason: Improves merchant comprehension and visual quality while preserving one runtime/persistence authority and keeping previews bounded.

alternatives.summary: Create a separate visual preset database/marketplace with arbitrary merchant widgets.
alternatives.reason: Would create a parallel authority, undermine Guarded Freedom and dramatically increase performance/security/regression surface.

specialistReviews.finding: Library 2.0 must be a presentation/indexing layer over existing preset/page-template authorities, not a new content authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Introduce pure semantic descriptor helpers and lightweight preview components; insertion still calls the existing canonical functions.

specialistReviews.finding: A visually rich gallery can accidentally mount dozens of live storefront runtimes or traverse arbitrarily deep preset trees on every render.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use bounded pure descriptors and CSS semantic thumbnails; cap structural inspection and never mount StorefrontRuntimeRenderer in Library cards.

specialistReviews.finding: Generic cube/line cards do not communicate what will be inserted and make the Builder feel registry-driven.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use recognizable section/element/page-template preview archetypes, curated categories, search and an explicit larger preview surface.

specialistReviews.finding: Search/filter UI must not expose a hidden insert path for disallowed components or Pro-only capability.
specialistReviews.resolution: Derive candidate sets from the same contextual/capability-filtered authorities first, then apply visual search/category filtering only to that safe set.

challenge.scenario: A template exposes 80 presets and each card renders a live runtime preview.
challenge.finding: The Library becomes slower than the storefront and creates massive DOM/listener cost.
challenge.resolution: Semantic CSS thumbnails only; no StorefrontRuntimeRenderer inside Library cards and larger preview remains the same bounded descriptor.

challenge.scenario: A deep preset fragment recursively walks thousands of descendants to create a thumbnail.
challenge.finding: Preview cost could be attacker/template amplified.
challenge.resolution: Descriptor traversal uses an explicit node inspection budget and returns a safe generic preview when the budget is exhausted.

challenge.scenario: A user searches for a commerce component hidden by current profile/capability.
challenge.finding: A secondary search index could leak an insertion route.
challenge.resolution: Search operates only on the already filtered safe candidate list; classification never grants insertability.

challenge.scenario: A section card looks like a Hero but insertion materializes a different authority or opaque widget.
challenge.finding: Visual Library could become misleading and non-editable.
challenge.resolution: Preview is derived from canonical fragment/component keys and insertion materializes ordinary editable native nodes through existing preset functions.

challenge.scenario: Factory presets and merchant Saved Blocks are shown as one undifferentiated collection.
challenge.finding: Ownership, lifecycle and trust become ambiguous.
challenge.resolution: Keep separate top-level surfaces and explicit source badges; no combined persistence model.

challenge.scenario: Page-template cards reimplement apply/create behavior inside the visual preview layer.
challenge.finding: Would duplicate page authority and optimistic concurrency rules.
challenge.resolution: Visual cards only call existing StorefrontPageTemplatesPanel actions/applyStorefrontPageTemplate paths.

challenge.scenario: Unknown future component keys break thumbnail rendering.
challenge.finding: Forward-compatible templates could crash the Library.
challenge.resolution: Classification fails to a generic bounded preview without affecting canonical insertion eligibility.

challenge.scenario: Mobile tries to show desktop-sized multi-column gallery cards and creates horizontal scroll.
challenge.finding: Mobile audit becomes visibly broken even though desktop is primary.
challenge.resolution: Responsive Library CSS collapses grids and keeps actions/touch targets inside the panel without introducing separate content semantics.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the committed active plan before product implementation.
Add unit coverage for bounded semantic classification, category/search behavior and unknown-component fallback.
Extend preset-library regression coverage to prove visual metadata never replaces canonical insertion/materialization.
Extend Builder completion coverage to prove element cards use semantic previews and no Library card imports/mounts StorefrontRuntimeRenderer.
Run existing preset/page-template/Saved Block and capability regression suites through Incremental Replay.
Run typecheck and production build on exact implementation HEAD.
Run Template Factory Quality Gate/browser proof to catch responsive/visual/runtime regressions.
Close only after exact-head Completion Truth Gate evidence; no main merge or golden update in this slice.

requirements.requirement: Implement one shared visual Library descriptor/preview layer for Sections, Elements and Page Templates without introducing a second content or renderer authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Library cards must not mount StorefrontRuntimeRenderer or create a new preset/page persistence path.

requirements.requirement: Upgrade Section Presets with semantic thumbnails, search, curated categories and a bounded larger preview with canonical one-click insertion.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Section insertion must continue through insertStorefrontSectionPreset and canonical validation.

requirements.requirement: Upgrade Element insertion cards with recognizable semantic previews while preserving contextual/product-profile/capability filtering.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Search/category filtering cannot make an otherwise disallowed element insertable.

requirements.requirement: Upgrade Page Template cards to the same visual language while retaining existing apply and create-page authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No page-template action or page document authority is duplicated in the preview layer.

requirements.requirement: Keep Factory Presets and merchant Saved Blocks as visibly and technically separate ownership/lifecycle surfaces.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No combined storage or trust model is created for factory and tenant-owned blocks.

requirements.requirement: Keep Library preview work bounded and lightweight for large template catalogs and deep preset fragments.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No unbounded recursive preview traversal or live runtime-per-card strategy is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Preserve Desktop-first authoring with polished responsive Library behavior on mobile without horizontal control overflow or a mobile-only document model.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Library responsiveness must not create duplicate breakpoint/page authorities.

requirements.requirement: Preserve Guarded Freedom and canonical runtime/performance/security boundaries while improving visual discoverability.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No arbitrary HTML/JS widget marketplace, gate weakening, golden update or main merge occurs.

notes: PO authorized continued VX Builder development while full desktop audit is deferred until the user has desktop hardware again. This slice addresses the visibly primitive Library/element-add experience without treating mobile as full authoring authority. No main merge and no golden update. Plan Before Code planned-projection currently resolves only existing admin-surface files; new Builder/Core files do not exist yet and therefore are not projected into Atlas authority scope. The pre-code expectation is intentionally DOMAIN-ADMIN/admin-operations and will be reconciled immediately after the first implementation commit when the actual diff contains the new Core files. Actual implementation diff now contains the new Core/Library files, so Atlas scope has expanded to the intended DOMAIN-ADMIN / DOMAIN-BUILDER / DOMAIN-STOREFRONT and matching admin-operations / builder-template-system / shared-storefront authorities. The plan is reconciled to actual implementation scope before verification.
